description: Comprehensive library of consulting frameworks used by McKinsey, BCG, Bain, and other top firms. Includes strategic, financial, operational, and problem-solving frameworks with implementation guidance.

portersFiveForces.name: Porter's Five Forces
portersFiveForces.author: Michael Porter (Harvard Business School)
portersFiveForces.purpose: Analyze industry structure and competitive intensity to determine attractiveness

forces.name: Threat of New Entrants
questions: How difficult is it for new competitors to enter this market?
How quickly can new entrants achieve scale?

forces.name: Bargaining Power of Suppliers
questions: How concentrated is the supplier base?
Can suppliers easily switch to other customers?

forces.name: Bargaining Power of Buyers
questions: Can buyers easily switch to competitors?

forces.name: Threat of Substitutes
questions: What alternative products/services can meet the same need?
How do substitutes compare on price and performance?
How likely are customers to switch?

forces.name: Rivalry Among Existing Competitors
questions: What is the rate of industry growth?

output.attractivenessScore: Calculate weighted score across all five forces
output.strategicImplications: Identify which forces are most favorable/unfavorable
output.recommendations: Strategies to improve positioning within the force framework

portersFiveForces.visualization: Radar chart showing strength of each force, or table with ratings and commentary

bcgMatrix.name: BCG Growth-Share Matrix
bcgMatrix.author: Boston Consulting Group
bcgMatrix.purpose: Prioritize resource allocation across business units or product lines based on market growth and relative market share

axes.horizontal: Relative Market Share (company share / largest competitor share)

quadrants.name: Cash Cows
quadrants.strategy: Harvest - milk for cash to fund Stars and Question Marks

quadrants.name: Question Marks (Problem Children)
quadrants.strategy: Selective investment - invest heavily or divest

calculation.relativeMarketShare: Your market share ÷ Largest competitor's market share

strategicImplications.balanced: Healthy mix of Stars, Cash Cows, and selective Question Marks
strategicImplications.unbalanced: Too many Dogs or Question Marks without Stars/Cash Cows
strategicImplications.resourceAllocation: Cash from Cows funds Stars; selective investment in Question Marks

bcgMatrix.visualization: 2x2 scatter plot with bubbles sized by revenue

mckinsey7S.name: McKinsey 7S Framework
mckinsey7S.author: McKinsey & Company (Peters, Waterman, Phillips)
mckinsey7S.purpose: Analyze organizational alignment across seven interdependent elements

hard.name: Structure
hard.description: How the organization is organized (hierarchy, reporting)

hard.name: Systems
hard.description: Processes and procedures (IT, HR, finance, operations)
questions: Do they enable or hinder strategy?

soft.name: Shared Values
soft.description: Core values and culture (center of model)

soft.name: Skills
questions: What are we really good at?
Do we have the skills to execute strategy?

soft.name: Staff
questions: Do we have the right people?

application.organizationalChange: Assess current vs desired state across all 7S
application.mergers: Identify cultural and operational integration challenges
application.strategy: Ensure all elements support strategic direction

mckinsey7S.visualization: Circular diagram with Shared Values in center, other 6S around it, interconnecting lines

geMcKinseyMatrix.name: GE-McKinsey Nine-Box Matrix
geMcKinseyMatrix.author: General Electric & McKinsey & Company
geMcKinseyMatrix.purpose: More nuanced portfolio analysis than BCG Matrix, using multi-factor assessment

scoring.weighting: Assign weights based on importance (sum to 100%)
scoring.calculation: Weighted average score for each axis

geMcKinseyMatrix.visualization: 3x3 grid with colored zones, bubbles for business units

swot.name: SWOT Analysis
swot.purpose: Identify Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats to inform strategy

strategies: SO (Strength-Opportunity): Leverage strengths to capture opportunities
WO (Weakness-Opportunity): Overcome weaknesses to pursue opportunities
ST (Strength-Threat): Use strengths to mitigate threats
WT (Weakness-Threat): Defensive strategies to minimize exposure

limitations: Can be too broad without prioritization
Should lead to actionable strategies, not just list-making

pestel.name: PESTEL Analysis
pestel.purpose: Analyze external macro factors affecting the organization

factors.name: Political
questions: How stable is the political environment?

factors.name: Economic
questions: How sensitive are we to economic cycles?

factors.name: Technological
questions: Are we keeping pace with innovation?

factors.name: Legal
questions: What legal requirements must we meet?

output.format: Table or list of factors with impact assessment (High/Medium/Low) and trends (Increasing/Stable/Decreasing)
output.strategicImplications: How to respond to each significant factor

valueChain.name: Porter's Value Chain
valueChain.author: Michael Porter
valueChain.purpose: Identify sources of competitive advantage by analyzing activities that create value

primary.name: Inbound Logistics
primary.optimization: Reduce costs, improve quality of inputs

analysis.costAnalysis: Identify where costs are incurred in each activity
analysis.differentiationAnalysis: Identify activities that create customer value and differentiation
analysis.benchmarking: Compare performance in each activity vs competitors

output.visualization: Horizontal arrow diagram with support activities above, primary activities below
output.recommendations: Where to invest, where to optimize, potential outsourcing candidates

ansoffMatrix.name: Ansoff Growth Matrix
ansoffMatrix.author: Igor Ansoff
ansoffMatrix.purpose: Identify growth strategies based on market and product dimensions

quadrants.name: Market Penetration
quadrants.strategy: Increase share in current markets with current products

quadrants.name: Market Development
quadrants.strategy: Enter new markets or segments with current products

quadrants.name: Product Development
quadrants.strategy: Develop new products for existing markets

quadrants.name: Diversification
quadrants.strategy: Enter new markets with new products

ansoffMatrix.visualization: 2x2 matrix with axes: Market (Existing/New) and Product (Existing/New)

dcf.name: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Valuation
dcf.purpose: Value an investment based on projected future cash flows discounted to present value
dcf.formula: PV = CF1/(1+r)^1 + CF2/(1+r)^2 + ... + CFn/(1+r)^n + Terminal Value/(1+r)^n
steps: Project Free Cash Flows (FCF) for forecast period (5-10 years)
Determine Discount Rate (WACC for company, required return for project)
Calculate Terminal Value (perpetuity growth or exit multiple)
Discount all cash flows to present value
Sum to get Enterprise Value, adjust for debt/cash to get Equity Value

keyInputs.terminalGrowth: Perpetuity growth rate (typically GDP growth rate, 2-3%)

dcf.sensitivity: Run scenarios varying WACC (±1-2%), revenue growth (±5-10%), terminal value assumptions

irr.name: Internal Rate of Return (IRR)
irr.purpose: Calculate the discount rate at which NPV = 0, used to evaluate project profitability
irr.formula: Find r where: 0 = CF0 + CF1/(1+r)^1 + CF2/(1+r)^2 + ... + CFn/(1+r)^n

interpretation.hurdle: IRR must exceed hurdle rate (WACC + risk premium)
interpretation.comparison: Compare IRR across mutually exclusive projects

limitations: Can have multiple IRRs for unconventional cash flows
Doesn't account for project scale (prefer NPV for that)

npv.name: Net Present Value (NPV)
npv.purpose: Calculate the value created by an investment (PV of inflows - PV of outflows)
advantages: Accounts for time value of money

payback.name: Payback Period
payback.purpose: Time required to recover initial investment
payback.calculation: Count years until cumulative cash flows equal initial investment

interpretation.discounted: Uses discounted cash flows for more accurate payback

payback.usage: Quick screening tool, especially for high-risk or short-horizon projects

roi.name: Return on Investment (ROI)
roi.purpose: Simple profitability metric comparing gain to investment

sensitivityAnalysis.name: Sensitivity Analysis
sensitivityAnalysis.purpose: Test impact of changes in key variables on financial outcomes (NPV, IRR)

method.oneWay: Vary one variable at a time (e.g., revenue ±10%), hold others constant
method.twoWay: Vary two variables simultaneously, show in matrix
method.scenario: Define discrete scenarios (Base, Optimistic, Pessimistic) with multiple variable changes

output.tornado: Tornado diagram showing which variables have biggest impact
output.table: Sensitivity table with NPV/IRR for different scenarios
output.chart: Waterfall chart showing contribution of each variable to total variance

mece.name: MECE Principle
mece.author: McKinsey & Company
mece.purpose: Structure analysis to avoid overlaps and gaps

examples.revenue: MECE: Product A + Product B + Product C (if these are all products)

issueTree.name: Issue Tree / Logic Tree
issueTree.purpose: Decompose a problem into MECE sub-issues to identify root causes and solutions

structure.branches: MECE decomposition of root into sub-issues

types.diagnostic: What is causing the problem? (e.g., Why are profits declining?)
types.solution: How can we solve the problem? (e.g., How to increase revenue?)

bestPractices: Go 3-5 levels deep (not too shallow, not too deep)
Validate hypotheses at leaf level with data

hypothesisDriven.name: Hypothesis-Driven Problem Solving
hypothesisDriven.purpose: Start with a hypothesis about the answer, then test it (vs. boiling the ocean)
process: Develop initial hypothesis based on experience/intuition
Identify what data/analysis would prove/disprove hypothesis
hypothesisDriven.example: If we reduce prices by 10%, then volume will increase by 20%, because price elasticity in this segment is -2.0

pyramidPrinciple.name: Pyramid Principle
pyramidPrinciple.author: Barbara Minto (McKinsey)
pyramidPrinciple.purpose: Structure communication with the answer first, then supporting arguments

scqa.name: SCQA Framework
scqa.author: Barbara Minto (McKinsey)
scqa.purpose: Structure storytelling to engage audience and drive to recommendation

components.name: Situation
components.example: Our company has 15% market share in a $500M market

components.name: Complication
components.example: However, a new competitor entered with 10% lower prices

components.name: Question
components.example: How should we respond to maintain share and profitability?

components.name: Answer
components.example: We recommend a three-pronged response: cost reduction, differentiation, and selective price matching

variations.multipleComplications: Can have multiple complications before the question

adkar.name: ADKAR Model
adkar.author: Prosci

stages.name: Awareness
actions: Share data on need for change

stages.name: Desire
actions: Address WIIFM (What's In It For Me)

adkar.application: Assess where individuals/groups are stuck in ADKAR progression and address barriers

kotter8Step.name: Kotter's 8-Step Change Model
kotter8Step.author: John Kotter (Harvard)
steps: Create Vision (clear picture of future state)
Empower Action (remove barriers, enable change agents)
Build on Change (use momentum, tackle bigger issues)
Anchor in Culture (embed changes in processes, norms)

frameworkSelection.strategic: Use Porter's Five Forces for industry analysis, BCG/GE Matrix for portfolio decisions, McKinsey 7S for organizational alignment
frameworkSelection.financial: Use DCF for valuation, NPV for project selection, IRR for profitability comparison, Sensitivity for risk assessment
frameworkSelection.problemSolving: Use MECE for structure, Issue Trees for problem decomposition, Hypothesis-Driven for fast problem solving, Pyramid Principle for communication

usageGuidelines.combining: Often use multiple frameworks in sequence (e.g., PESTEL → Porter's Five Forces → SWOT → Strategy Selection)
usageGuidelines.customization: Adapt frameworks to context - don't force-fit if not relevant
usageGuidelines.documentation: Always document assumptions, data sources, and scoring methodologies
usageGuidelines.iteration: Revisit frameworks periodically as conditions change
